ui.mesh.approval.credential_title.role: heading — mesh approval card, credential request with no server-provided summary
ui.mesh.approval.credential_title.tone: Plain and factual; a neutral label, not a warning
ui.mesh.approval.credential_title.note: The card's heading when the server sent a CREDENTIAL access request but no summary line, so this stands as the title. It names the CATEGORY of request, not the specific credential, and it is not a grant: the card's own approve/deny controls are what ask for the decision. Length: this is the card's LEAD body line (`text-body-sm`, below the state line), so it carries the card - keep it to a couple of words, around the English footprint; an over-long title wraps the card's longest line. Do not expand it into a sentence and do not name a credential the server did not name.

ui.mesh.approval.unknown_title.role: heading — mesh approval card, request whose kind the app does not recognise
ui.mesh.approval.unknown_title.tone: Plain and factual; neutral fallback, not an error or a warning
ui.mesh.approval.unknown_title.note: The card's heading when the server sends an approval request of a kind this app version does not understand and gave no summary, so this stands as the title. It is a FALLBACK, not a failure: the request is still real and still decidable elsewhere, so keep it neutral rather than alarming. Length: this is the card's LEAD body line (`text-body-sm`, below the state line), so it carries the card - a couple of words, around the English footprint; an over-long title wraps the card's longest line. Do not turn it into an error message.

ui.mesh.approval.details_unavailable.role: status text — mesh approval card details section, no detail lines to show
ui.mesh.approval.details_unavailable.tone: Factual and restrained; a plain statement of absence
ui.mesh.approval.details_unavailable.note: Stands inside the card's details section when the request carried no detail lines to list, so the section says so rather than rendering empty. It is not an error and not a permission statement - it states that no description was provided. THE ENGLISH ITSELF CARRIES BOTH HALVES and both must survive: the absence ("The full request details are unavailable in this app.") AND the remedy ("Review the request from the command line on this machine."). Keep `this machine` uncompromised, and do not translate this into a bare "no details" line - the command-line sentence is the reader's way forward, and this string is the only place it appears for a request with no detail lines. Length: two short sentences where a list would have been; the surrounding section is `text-meta` and muted.

ui.mesh.approval.cli_review.role: instruction — mesh approval card, restricted request that must be reviewed at the command line
ui.mesh.approval.cli_review.tone: Plain and factual; an instruction, not a refusal and not an apology
ui.mesh.approval.cli_review.note: Shown on a still-pending request the app cannot decide here (an opaque credential/unknown kind, or `canApproveHere` false) and for which the server sent no `approve_remedy` text, so this is the generic remedy. It must stay TRUE: the app genuinely cannot approve it, and the command line on THIS machine genuinely can. Keep `command line` and `on this machine` uncompromised - a translation that drops either sends the reader to a surface that cannot help. Length: an explanatory line under the card, may wrap onto two lines; `text-meta` and muted, so keep it near the English length where the language allows.

ui.mesh.approval.approved_pending_apply.role: status label — mesh approval card, credential request approved but not yet applied
ui.mesh.approval.approved_pending_apply.tone: Factual and restrained; a state statement, not a progress indicator
ui.mesh.approval.approved_pending_apply.note: Replaces the card's normal state line for exactly one case: a credential request whose state is `approved` in the store, where approval is recorded but the apply step has not happened yet. There is no count and no time in it. THIS IS A LIE IF ENLARGED: it must not promise that access now works - approval and apply are two steps and only the second grants use. Length: one short state line in the card header, around the English footprint; it stands where the card's ordinary state word stands, so it may be slightly longer than a single word but must not wrap into a second line.

ui.mesh.approval.approved_apply_hint.role: instruction — mesh approval card, approved credential request with server-provided details
ui.mesh.approval.approved_apply_hint.tone: Plain and factual; points onward without promising the outcome
ui.mesh.approval.approved_apply_hint.note: Shown after a credential request is approved, when the server DID send detail lines, so the apply step exists to open. It points the reader at Details rather than telling them access is live: approval is recorded, apply is separate. Keep the reference to Details (the card's own disclosure control) - a translation that renames it sends the reader to a control that does not exist under that name. No placeholders. Length: an explanatory line under the card, may wrap; keep the two short sentences.

ui.mesh.approval.approved_details_missin.role: status text — mesh approval card, approved credential request whose details did not arrive
ui.mesh.approval.approved_details_missin.tone: Factual and restrained; states the gap without blaming the reader or the server
ui.mesh.approval.approved_details_missin.note: The sibling of `approved_apply_hint` for the case where approval is recorded but the server sent NO detail lines, so there is nothing to open. It must not imply the reader can do the apply step here - unlike its sibling it should NOT send them to Details for content that is absent. No placeholders. Length: an explanatory line under the card, may wrap; keep it to the same footprint as `approved_apply_hint` so the two variants do not shift the card's height.

ui.mesh.approval.request_window.role: status text — mesh approval card, credential request's remaining decision window
ui.mesh.approval.request_window.tone: Factual and restrained; quiet, secondary to the card's state
ui.mesh.approval.request_window.note: The countdown beside a still-decidable credential request. Placeholder: `remaining` is an ALREADY-LOCALIZED string produced by the meshes' own `approvalRemainingLabel`, which picks one of the sibling `expires_*` messages (under a minute / minutes / hours) - it is never a raw number here. Do not reformat it, pluralize it, add units to it, or wrap it in `{remaining, number}`: that work is already done by those sibling keys, and doing it again would double the unit or the plural. Length: a compact line (`text-meta`, dim) in the card header, around the English footprint. Keep the trailing colon of the English label; the duration reads after it. Note the sibling `expires_*` keys carry the plural forms, so a locale's plural categories belong to THEM, not to this label.
